items.title: Section: Four Virtues of a Composer — Freedom from Arrogance, and Great Compassion

items.zh: 將造論時，要以四德先自安處，乃可造論。一、於昔諸師應離憍慢；二、於有情類當起大悲；三、於同法者深生敬愛；四、不欲彰己有勝技能。云何於昔諸師應離憍慢？謂造論時，無如是心：古昔諸師尚能造論，況我今者當不造耶。要離如是憍慢染心，乃應造論。云何於有情類當起大悲？謂造論時，作如是觀：若不造論，無量有情於諸善法定當退失，又餘情類墮生老病，乃至廣說。是諸有情因我造論，若能解了乃至一句善說妙義，如是如是當奉行者，彼於長夜必獲大義利益安樂。要發如是增上心已，乃應造論。
items.en: When about to compose a treatise, one must first settle oneself in four virtues before one may compose: freedom from arrogance towards the masters of former times; great compassion towards beings; deep reverence and affection towards fellow practitioners of the same Dharma; and no wish to display one's own superior skill. What is freedom from arrogance towards the masters of former times? It means that when composing, one holds no such thought as: since the masters of old were able to compose, how could I possibly fail to compose now. One must be free of this arrogant and defiled attitude before one may compose. What is great compassion towards beings? It means that when composing, one reflects: if the treatise is not composed, countless beings will surely regress from wholesome dharma, and other beings besides will fall into birth, old age, sickness, and so on at length. Any being who, because of my composing, comes to understand and practice even a single well-spoken phrase of its subtle meaning will surely obtain great benefit and ease through the long night of saṃsāra. One must generate this exalted resolve before one may compose.

items.zh: 云何於同法者深生敬愛？謂造論時，作如是觀：若不造論，為欲利他諸同法者，於利他事定當退失。云何不欲彰己有勝技能？謂造論時，無如是心：當令世間咸謂於我聰叡明哲，能造論者、開闡義者，深生淨信，因此多獲利養恭敬。但為自他善根增長，以無染心，乃可造論。

items.title: Section: Five Similes for Why a Treatise Is Called an Adornment of the Sutra

items.zh: 復次，此中如實開示如來所說經義，名莊嚴經。譬如紅蓮，其花未開，雖生歡喜，不如敷榮。又如真金，未為嚴具，雖生歡喜，不如成功。又如美膳，未及得食，雖生歡喜，不如已食。又如慶書，未暇開覽，雖生歡喜，不如披閱。又如珍寶，未得現前，雖生歡喜，不如已得現前受用。如是如來所說經義若未顯發，雖生歡喜，不如開示。故說造論名莊嚴經。
items.en: Furthermore, faithfully opening up and displaying the meaning of what the Tathāgata taught in the sutras is called adorning the sutra. It is like a red lotus: while its flower has not yet opened, though joy arises, it does not compare to its full blossoming. It is like true gold: before it is fashioned into an ornament, though joy arises, it does not compare to its completion. It is like a fine meal: before one gets to eat it, though joy arises, it does not compare to having already eaten it. It is like an auspicious book: before there is leisure to open and read it, though joy arises, it does not compare to actually perusing it. It is like a treasure: before it is obtained and present, though joy arises, it does not compare to already having obtained it and being able to use it. Just so, if the meaning the Tathāgata taught in the sutras has not yet been made manifest, though joy arises, it does not compare to having it opened up and shown. Therefore it is said that composing a treatise is called adorning the sutra.

items.title: Section: Opening the Science of Linguistics — Seven Kinds of Penetrating Understanding

items.zh: 復次，略有七種通達。一、字通達，二、字義通達，三、能取通達，四、能取義通達，五、繫縛通達，六、解脫通達，七、法性通達。字通達者，通達為常。字義通達者，達為無常。
items.en: Furthermore, briefly, there are seven kinds of penetrating understanding: penetrating the syllable, penetrating the syllable's meaning, penetrating the grasping faculty, penetrating the grasping faculty's object, penetrating bondage, penetrating liberation, and penetrating the nature of dharmas. Penetrating the syllable means penetrating it as constant. Penetrating the syllable's meaning means penetrating it as impermanent.

items.zh: 能取通達者，謂根識等，達安立諦或非安立。如能取通達，能取義通達，當知亦爾。繫縛通達者，通達相縛、或麁重縛。與此相違，當知說名解脫通達。

items.title: Section: Penetrating the Very Nature of Dharmas, Closing the Science of Linguistics

items.zh: 法性通達者，謂能通達法性安住、法界安住，非從自在、自性、士夫中間等有。
items.en: Penetrating the nature of dharmas means penetrating the abiding of dharma-nature and the abiding of the dharma-realm, understanding that dharmas do not arise from Īśvara, from a primordial self-nature, from a creator-person, or from an intervening Brahmā. The above is the brief decisive discernment of linguistics; since the Ground of Wisdom Attained through Hearing itself treats linguistics only briefly, its decisive discernment is likewise brief.

items.title: Section: Ten Marks of Complete Learning, and the Fascicle's Own Closing Declaration

items.zh: 復次，由十相故，具足多聞。謂善說者說故，顯了文句說故，盡其所有、如其所有義說故，安樂方便加行說故，離眾苦說故。如是五種。復有五種。謂不求過失而聽法故，但求涅槃而聽法故，善聽法故，諦聽法故，於依名句文身義審諦觀察而聽法故。於此地中餘決擇文，更不復現。
items.en: Furthermore, by ten marks, one becomes fully accomplished in vast learning: the Dharma taught by a skilled speaker, its phrases made clear, taught exhaustively and truly, taught together with the means to ease, and taught so as to free beings from suffering. And a further five: hearing without seeking fault, hearing solely for nirvana, hearing well, hearing attentively, and hearing with careful examination of the meaning carried in name, phrase, and letter. Within this ground, no further text of decisive discernment appears.

blocks.text: A short day on the ethics of writing, and the science of language.

No arrogance towards former masters, compassion, reverence for fellow practitioners, and no wish to display skill. (Untranslated, 0658a29: one writes because, if one did not, fellow practitioners would lose benefit; and never with the thought "let the world call me brilliant and give me offerings", but only for the growth of good roots in oneself and others, with an unstained mind.)

The red lotus, true gold, a fine meal, an auspicious book, and a treasure. Master Cháng Bǎi: the bud is the Buddha's sūtra and the opened flower the treatise: a treatise opens out the sūtra's meaning.

Master Cháng Bǎi: penetrating 字 means penetrating it as constant; among name, phrase, and letter, it is the letter. (Untranslated, 0658b20: understanding the grasping faculties and consciousnesses, the bonds of marks and of coarse heaviness, and liberation from them.)

The refuges, the many senses of truth, the Buddha's silences, and the ethics of writing. For anyone who writes about the Dharma, the four virtues of a writer are a good checklist: no arrogance, compassion, respect, and no wish to show off.

quiz.q: What are the four virtues in which one settles before composing?
options: that the teaching circulate, beings enter the Dharma, lost meanings reopen, and scattered ones be condensed
pure body, speech, mind, and compassion
perfect speech, fearlessness, dignity, and worthiness
no arrogance towards former masters, compassion, reverence for fellow practitioners, and no wish to display skill
quiz.why: The treatise lists freedom from arrogance towards former masters, compassion, reverence for fellow practitioners, and no wish to display skill. The motives are a separate list of six. Only the first two virtues are expanded in the English.

quiz.q: Which comparisons does the treatise give for adorning the sūtra?
options: a torrent's waves, a mirror's images, a dream, a mirage, and a plantain stem
seed, soil, rain, sunlight, and harvest
a red lotus opening, gold fashioned, a meal eaten, a book read, a treasure used
prescription, doctor, patient, nurse, and cure
quiz.why: The treatise gives the red lotus, true gold, a fine meal, an auspicious book, and a treasure, then concludes that the meaning of the sūtras, until made manifest, does not compare to being opened up and shown.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi map sūtra and treatise in the red lotus comparison?
options: the bud stands for the sūtra, and the opened flower for the treatise
the opened flower is the sūtra and the bud the treatise
red is compassion and white is wisdom
the lotus is the Buddha and the mud is beings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the bud stands for the Buddha's sūtra and the opened flower for the treatise. A treatise opens out the meaning of the sūtra, and for that reason it is called adorning the sūtra.

quiz.q: "Penetrating the word means penetrating it as constant." Why does this not work?
options: 字 is the letter of 文身, which does not shift; it is not a word
it works: word means 字, each word being eternally unchanging, a basic claim of linguistics and the Buddhist position too
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: penetrating 字 means penetrating it as constant, and among name, phrase, and letter it is the letter. A word carries meaning, which is treated as impermanent, so word obscures why 字 is called constant.
